instruction:
Create apps/api/src/task/controllers/update-task-estimated-hours.ts.
Mirror update-task-due-date.ts exactly in structure, but publish the EXISTING event "task.updated" instead of a new event type.

async function updateTaskEstimatedHours({ id, estimatedHours, currentUserId }: { id: string; estimatedHours: number | null; currentUserId: string; })

Body:
1. read-before-write: db.query.taskTable.findFirst({ where: eq(taskTable.id, id) }); if missing throw new HTTPException(404, { message: "Task not found" }).
2. db.update(taskTable).set({ estimatedHours }).where(eq(taskTable.id, id)).returning(); destructure const [updatedTask].
3. if (!updatedTask) throw new HTTPException(500, { message: "Failed to update task estimated hours" }).
4. await publishEvent("task.updated", { taskId: updatedTask.id, projectId: updatedTask.projectId, title: updatedTask.title, status: updatedTask.status, userId: currentUserId });
5. return updatedTask.
export default updateTaskEstimatedHours;

Set estimatedHours directly (it is already number | null after validation) - do NOT use "estimatedHours || null" because that would turn a legitimate 0 into null.
Do NOT invent a new event type. Do NOT add an activity row.

describe("API integration: task estimated hours", ...) with its own beforeEach database reset, following the existing file's exact patterns for creating a workspace member, a project fixture, mocking the authenticated session and building the app.

Cases:
1. POST /api/task/:projectId WITHOUT estimatedHours returns 200, response estimatedHours is null, persisted row is null.
2. POST with estimatedHours 2.5 returns 200, response 2.5, persisted 2.5, and typeof the returned value is "number" (this asserts drizzle mode:"number"; a regression to mode:"string" must fail here).
3. PUT /api/task/estimated-hours/:id with 0.5 -> 200 and 0.5; then 3.25 -> 200 and 3.25; then null -> 200 and null. Set, change and clear in one case.

8. THE CRITICAL REGRESSION: set an estimate via PUT /api/task/estimated-hours/:id, then send PUT /api/task/:id WITHOUT estimatedHours (simulating a kanban drag which replaces the whole task), then assert the estimate SURVIVED. A naive unconditional set in updateTask would null it here.
